compensating.why: hop 3 takes an end of 0 as absent
hop 3 scans the ends from the first field
the facade puts the disk start before the relative header offset

ownership_reason: Only the gold knows how much room each field of the record takes and decides where it ends: it gives every field its end (-1 for an absent one) from a running end that advances by the field's place-dependent width. Hop 3 reads the gold's ends and returns the last one that is not -1; hops 1, 2 and 4 pass the fields and the length along; no caller holds a width. Once the gold has advanced the running end past the absent relative header offset, the disk start ends at 28 and the length 28 follows; 20 can come out of the chain only if a caller recomputes the widths itself, and re-ordering or dropping fields at the facade puts the disk start at an eight-byte place. The gold's javadoc promises where each field ends in a record that holds the given fields in the given order; a record holding the original size, the compressed size and the disk start holds the disk start from 16 to 20. The convention that an absent field of the ZIP64 extended information extra field does not appear is pinned outside the gold: the class javadoc (the fields only appear if the corresponding directory field is set), the intact siblings getCentralDirectoryData (the write offset advances only past a present value), reparseCentralDirectoryData and parseFromLocalFileData (the read offset advances only past a present value), and the passing tests testReadLFHSizesAndDisk (disk start read at 16 without a relative header offset), testReadCDSomethingAndDisk (disk start read at 8 of 12 bytes), and, through the chain, testWriteCDSizeAndOffset and testWriteCDOnlySizes.
